correctness.rationale: The replacement corrects the literal homology claim to reduced integral homology; in ordinary homology these nonempty connected wedges also have H0=Z. The join and homotopy type are unchanged. Fixed barycentric coordinates are constant on the edge orbits, and summing the coordinates on each orbit inverts its barycenter map simplex by simplex. Within a permuted block the internal complete graph is forbidden unless it is a single edge; between two permuted blocks K_{k_i,k_j} contains C4. Edges to a single fixed vertex are one star. Two distinct stars of one block form C4, and a star together with its internal edge forms a triangle. Conversely the allowed stars attach at only one vertex each, so the forest condition is precisely the asserted join, with D0 the empty-face-only factor. This verifies all m=0,1,2 conventions and both examples. Matroid shellability gives the sphere wedge; the join with D_s is a wedge of s-1 suspensions. The forest count also follows independently: the signed Euler sum gives B_m=-m![z^m]exp(-R+R²/2) where R=ze^R is the rooted-tree EGF and R-R²/2 counts unrooted trees. Lagrange inversion gives (m-1)![u^{m-1}](1-u)exp((m-1)u+u²/2). The H recurrence reduces this to (m-2)H_{m-3}(m-1), including 1,6,51,560 for m=3..6.
residual_risks: The attached finite checker asserts the first three Euler values and prints all four; the exact generating-function derivation is independent of that assertion and of the inaccessible Jonsson passage.

value.rationale: This is a family-wide model of actual geometric fixed points for natural Young symmetries. The PL join identifies the dependence on block sizes, handles the empty and cone boundary cases, and isolates extra fixed points missed by selecting only individually fixed graph edges. Those are reusable structural conclusions rather than just a tabulation of ordinary forest counts.
residual_risks: No claim for arbitrary transitive actions, quotient complexes or an equivariant classification of the ambient forest complex.
